title: BP Texas City refinery explosion: process-safety warnings, personal-safety metric trap, and production-pressure impairment
summary: BP Texas City is added as a non-aerospace cross-domain test of the warning-governance pattern. CSB’s official materials identify the fatal ISOM-unit startup explosion and emphasize organizational causes: process-safety warning signals, audits, previous releases, maintenance/investment constraints, personal-safety metric focus, reporting/learning culture failure, and unreviewed organizational changes.

status_history.note: Seed listed BP Texas City among chemical/industrial engineering failures; added to queue and promoted with CSB sources.

type_payload.system: hydrocarbon isomerization unit, raffinate splitter tower, blowdown drum/stack, startup procedures, process safety management system

sequence_of_events.event: During ISOM unit startup, raffinate splitter tower flooding and overpressure developed.
Hydrocarbons were released through an atmospheric vent/blowdown stack and formed a flammable vapor cloud.
The vapor cloud ignited, causing explosions and fire; occupied trailers near the process unit were heavily affected.
CSB traced the event beyond startup actions to process-safety management, investment, metric, learning, and organizational-change failures.

type_payload.proximate_cause: Overfilled/overpressurized distillation tower leading to hydrocarbon release through an atmospheric vent/blowdown stack and vapor-cloud explosion.
warning_signals: previous serious releases from ISOM blowdown stack
process safety manager warnings and action-item concerns
personal-safety metric focus masking major accident risk
type_payload.proof_burden_observation: The safety signal portfolio was fragmented and could be outweighed by financial/personal-safety metrics unless translated into binding process-safety authority.
contributing_factors: cost-cutting and failure to invest impaired process safety
deficient process hazard analysis and process-safety information
occupied trailers sited too close to hazardous process unit
latent_conditions: Personal injury rate metrics can improve while catastrophic process risk worsens.
Organizational/budget changes can be safety-critical even when not treated as formal engineering changes.
decisions_that_mattered: Not effectively investigating earlier releases/startup anomalies.
Not using MOC to evaluate budget cuts, staffing, and organizational policy changes.
Not treating process-safety audits and warnings as requiring authoritative action.
type_payload.record_grain_warning: This is an official-report shell, not a full process-safety reconstruction or legal account.

handling_notes: Fifteen workers died and 180 were injured; avoid turning the event into a metric anecdote without human-sensitivity review.
Keep focus on system, process-safety, and organizational learning rather than operator blame.

unknowns: Full startup timeline and operator-interface data need extraction.
